title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a sketch of the full package of realization data that a Tannakian category of pure (probably semisimple) motives over Q, with good reduction over an open S ⊂ Spec(Z), should carry. In modern terms it is a 'system of realizations' together with the motivic Galois group. The aim is to describe the extra structures on the Tannakian category and the comparison relations between them.

(1) Betti fibre functor T_B (over Q, via an embedding of Q̄ into C). Its automorphism group is the motivic Galois group G over Q.

(2) ℓ-adic realization T_ℓ ≅ T_B ⊗_Q Q_ℓ (comparison of étale and singular cohomology). This gives a Galois representation π = Gal(Q̄/Q) → G(Q_ℓ), with ℓ written p on the page, unramified at the points of S other than ℓ. The places are p ∈ S (closed points) or ∞, with decomposition groups π(p) = Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p) → π and π(∞) = Z/2 (complex conjugation).

(3) Hodge-type cocharacters at each place.
- At ∞: two cocharacters i_1^(∞), i_2^(∞): G_m,C ⇉ G_C, the two factors of the Deligne torus giving the Hodge (p,q) bigrading.
- At p: two cocharacters i_1^(p), i_2^(p): G_m,C_p ⇉ G_{C_p}, the Hodge–Tate cocharacters of the p-adic realization.
- From these come subgroups U^(∞) ⊂ G_C and U' ⊂ G_{C_p}: the unipotent radicals of the parabolics fixing the associated filtrations (via i_2).

(4) De Rham fibre functor T_DR over Q, with automorphism group G'. Since both are fibre functors, P = Isom^⊗(T_B, T_DR) is a G-torsor (the period torsor) and G' = G^P is the inner twist ad(P). The Hodge filtration on T_DR gives cocharacters j_2: G_m,Q → G'. These are well defined only up to conjugation by the unipotent radical U' of the filtration parabolic: the splittings of the filtration form a torsor R under U'.

(5) Further structure on T_DR.
- For each closed point p ∈ S (good reduction), a crystalline Frobenius F_p ∈ G'(Q_p) (linear, since the residue field is F_p).
- At infinity, F_∞ ∈ G'(R) of order 2.

(6) Comparison data between T_B and T_DR.
- At ∞: a given point ρ^(∞) ∈ P(C), the classical period isomorphism H_B⊗C ≅ H_DR⊗C. It carries the class of j_2 (the Hodge filtration) to that of i_2^(∞).
- At p: for every splitting j_2 ∈ U' and every generator λ ∈ C_p(1)^* (a p-adic '2πi'), an element ρ^(p)(j_2, λ) ∈ P(C_p) carrying j_2 to i_2^(p). This is a map C_p(1)^* × U'(C_p) → P(C_p).
- The map must be equivariant for the natural action of C_p^* × U'(C_p) and compatible with π(p) = Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p).

In modern language, item (6) at p is exactly the Hodge–Tate comparison H_et ⊗ C_p ≅ ⊕_j gr^j H_DR ⊗ C_p(−j). Turning it into an isomorphism with ungraded H_DR ⊗ C_p requires choosing a splitting of the Hodge filtration and a trivialization of C_p(1). There is no Galois-invariant such isomorphism because C_p(1)^{G_{Q_p}} = 0, so the Galois compatibility must be twisted through λ. Grothendieck thus encodes the p-adic period comparison as a torsor-valued equivariant map. This is a precursor of Fontaine's period torsors, which avoid the choices by working over B_dR.
errors: The ℓ-adic prime is written p, and the transcription's 'T_R' should be the ℓ-adic realization T_ℓ ≅ T_B ⊗ Q_ℓ. Also, 'unramified in S − {p}' implicitly treats S as the good-reduction open set, which is consistent with Frobenius F_p being defined for closed p ∈ S.
F_∞ ∈ G'(R): Deligne's F_∞ naturally acts on Betti cohomology, i.e. lies in G(Q) or G(R). Placing it in G'(R) requires transport via the real structure / period comparison, which is not stated.
The phrase 'U' ⊂ G_{C^(p)}' at p is then reused as U' ⊂ G' over Q (the de Rham filtration unipotent radical), so the notation conflates the p-adic and de Rham versions. Harmless, but imprecise.
The Galois compatibility (b) for ρ^(p) cannot be naive invariance, since C_p(1) has no nonzero Galois-fixed vector. It must act on λ and on P(C_p) simultaneously. The page leaves this implicit.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group G as automorphisms of the Betti fibre functor on motives over Q with good reduction on S, plus Galois representation π → G(Q_ℓ)
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois group / Tannakian category of motives
ideas.where_published: Not written up by Grothendieck himself; developed in Saavedra's thesis under his direction and recalled in Récoltes et Semailles

ideas.what: De Rham fibre functor, the comparison torsor P = Isom(T_B, T_DR), and G' = G^P as an inner form
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor; de Rham motivic Galois group
ideas.where_published: Period ideas mentioned in Grothendieck's 1966 de Rham paper (footnote) and in Lang's book; Tannakian form in Deligne

ideas.what: Hodge filtration as a cocharacter defined up to its unipotent radical (splittings form a U'-torsor); Hodge cocharacters i_1, i_2 at ∞
ideas.where_published: Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes, Ch. IV–VI

ideas.what: p-adic comparison as an equivariant map C_p(1)^* × U'(C_p) → P(C_p) (depending on a filtration splitting and a p-adic 2πi), compatible with Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p)
ideas.modern_name: Hodge–Tate comparison / p-adic period torsor (precursor of B_dR periods)
ideas.where_published: Only the related 'mysterious functor' problem appears (ICM Nice 1970, Barsotti–Tate groups and crystals)

missed.claim: Around 1970 Grothendieck formulated a complete 'system of realizations' for motives over Q: Betti, ℓ-adic with ramification, de Rham with filtration, crystalline Frobenius, F_∞, and complex and p-adic comparison data. The p-adic comparison is phrased as a torsor-valued map depending on a splitting of the Hodge filtration and a generator of C_p(1). This anticipates Deligne's systems of realizations (1979) and the Tannakian shape of Fontaine's p-adic periods.
missed.quote: Pour tout j_2∈U', et tout λ∈C^(p)(1)^*, un élément ρ^(p)(j_2,λ)∈P(C^p) transformant j_2 en i_2 ... et compatibilité avec opérations de a) C^(p)*×U'(C^p) b) π(p)=Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck himself had the p-adic comparison as part of the motivic torsor picture, with a correct accounting of the needed choices, before Fontaine. This is historically relevant to the 'mysterious functor' story. Mathematically it is subsumed by B_dR theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Systems of realizations and motivic Galois groups are known to originate with Grothendieck. However, an explicit unpublished formulation with Hodge–Tate cocharacters, crystalline Frobenius in the de Rham group, and a choice-dependent p-adic period map from about 1970 is a notable historical detail. It is not new mathematics today.
transcription_corrections: 'T_R ≃ T_B ⊗_Q Q_ℓ' should read T_ℓ (ℓ-adic realization).
'π → G(Q_p)': here p plays the role of ℓ; 'non ramifié dans S−{p}'.
The marginal note at the left of i_1, i_2 is hard to read ('résultats des autres structures' is uncertain); it probably refers to filtrations/structures at the other places.
'(p pt fermé ou ∞)' refers to the place p of S ∪ {∞}.
Left-margin brace labels read T_B, T_DR, and 'relations entre T_B et T_DR'; 'Élément donné' introduces ρ^(∞).
